title: bug: every state.load() builds a new MentionRouter, so a FileWatcher reload clears the chat loop guard: a paused channel resumes routing and hop counts reset with no human message
description:
Filed by architect-1dd28c7c from the daemon/proxy defect hunt (task-8f18d6fa).

PROBLEM
The chat loop guard lives in MentionRouter: hopCounts, pausedChannels and maxHops, at packages/moe-daemon/src/util/mentionRouter.ts ~75-81. docs/SCHEMA.md:1758 says that when chatMaxAgentHops (default 4) is exceeded, "routing pauses until a human message resets the counter". mentionRouter.ts ~252-253 adds that only a human, or an explicit continue token, resumes a channel.

StateManager.load() breaks that. It ends with `this.mentionRouter = new MentionRouter(this.project?.settings?.chatMaxAgentHops ?? 4)` (state/StateManager.ts ~1132-1133). The new router exists only to apply the setting, but it throws away every channel's hop count and pause. The FileWatcher calls state.load() on every external .moe change that self-write suppression lets through (index.ts ~848-853). state/sweeps.ts ~172-182 records that on the live host a claim reliably produces such a reload (measured 2026-09-17), and git operations that touch tracked .moe files produce them too. So an agent-to-agent loop resumes after the next reload, which defeats the guard. The sweeps fix in that same comment handled this reset-on-reload class for the periodic timers, but not for the router.

EVIDENCE: repro on HEAD 99cae90a (a descendant of 1558f141), in a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout. It uses ToolTestHarness plus the real FileWatcher, wired exactly as index.ts wires it. File: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/zzHuntUtil1.test.ts (copy it into a snapshot's packages/moe-daemon/src/util/). Output: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/repro-output-util-99cae90a.txt.
Command: cd <snapshot>/packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/util/zzHuntUtil1.test.ts
Observed:
before reload: {"hopCount":5,"paused":true}
after reload : {"hopCount":0,"paused":false}
6th agent hop routed to: ["worker-a"]
hops 5-8 after reload routed: [["worker-b"],["worker-a"],["worker-b"],["worker-a"]] state: {"hopCount":4,"paused":false}
paused after 5 hops: {"hopCount":5,"paused":true}
reloads: 1 state now: {"hopCount":0,"paused":false}   (after an external write to .moe/tasks/task-ext.json, seen by the real FileWatcher)
next agent hop routed to: ["worker-a"]
Tests 3 failed (3)

FIX DIRECTION
Keep one MentionRouter for the daemon's lifetime:
- Give it a maxHops setter (e.g. setMaxHops(n); maxHops stops being readonly).
- Have load() call the setter on the existing router instead of constructing a new one. The first load still constructs it.
Hop counts and pauses then survive reloads, and a human message or the existing continue path still resets them. Keep load()'s existing error handling.
Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/util/mentionRouter.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts, plus one new test file (e.g. packages/moe-daemon/src/util/mentionRouter.reload.test.ts).
definitionOfDone: A channel paused by the loop guard stays paused across state.load(). A vitest case drives agent hops past chatMaxAgentHops, calls state.load(), and asserts that the next agent-to-agent message routes to [] and that mentionRouter.getChannelState still reports the channel paused.

Hop counts survive a reload and the setting still applies. One vitest case reaches 4 hops, reloads, and asserts the 5th hop pauses. Another lowers settings.chatMaxAgentHops in project.json, reloads, and asserts the new limit governs the following hops.

After a reload, a human message still resets the counter and un-pauses the channel. The existing mentionRouter, mentionRouterSystemHops and chatSystemFeed suites pass unchanged, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first (RED). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/mentionRouter.reload.test.ts with the Write tool; a global rail forbids shell writes to tracked files.

State-backed cases use ToolTestHarness from ../tools/toolTestHarness.js: h.init(); h.setupMoeFolder(); h.createWorker for worker-a and worker-b with status 'CODING'; await h.state.load(); take the #workers channel id from h.state.getChannels(). Add a helper hop(from, to) that returns (await h.state.sendMessage({ channel, sender: from, content: tag(to) + ' ping' })).routingTargets. Build the mention token at runtime as String.fromCharCode(64) + id. Never write a literal at-token in a plan or step text (mem:gotcha-plan-step-text-at-tokens-echoed-as-mentions).

Cases, all with exact assertions:
(a) A paused channel stays paused across state.load(). Four alternating hops each route to the other worker, and the 5th routes []. Then await h.state.load(). expect(h.state.mentionRouter.getChannelState(ch)).toEqual({ hopCount: 5, paused: true }), and the next agent hop routes [].
(b) Hop counts survive a reload. After 4 hops, load(), and getChannelState equals { hopCount: 4, paused: false }. The 5th hop routes [] and the channel is paused.
(c) A lowered limit applies on reload. Read path.join(h.moePath, 'project.json'), set settings.chatMaxAgentHops = 2, write it back, and await h.state.load(). Hops 1 and 2 route to the mentioned worker. Hop 3 routes [] and getChannelState reports paused.
(d) A human still resumes after a reload. Pause the channel with 5 hops, load(), then send as sender 'human' with no mention. getChannelState equals { hopCount: 0, paused: false }, and the next agent hop routes to the mentioned worker.
(e) MentionRouter unit, no state, reusing the makeWorker/makeMessage fixture shape from util/mentionRouterSystemHops.test.ts. Take new MentionRouter(4), route 3 agent hops, call setMaxHops(2), and the 4th hop returns paused true with hopCount 4. For each invalid input (0, -1, 2.5, NaN, undefined), a fresh router given setMaxHops(x) routes hops 1-4 and pauses at hop 5 (the default of 4).

Run the file in the step 3 snapshot. (a), (b) and (e) must fail on today's code. (c) and (d) pass today; they pin that the setting still applies and that a human still resets. Error handling: afterEach calls h.cleanup(), so the temp dir is removed even when an assertion throws.
implementationPlan.note: Wrote cases (a)-(e); RED run happens in the snapshot at the gate step.

implementationPlan.description:
Minimum fix, with the Edit tool only.

1) packages/moe-daemon/src/util/mentionRouter.ts:
- Make maxHops non-readonly.
- Add setMaxHops(maxHops: number | undefined): void. It stores maxHops when Number.isInteger(maxHops) && maxHops >= 1, and otherwise stores the default 4, the same default the constructor uses. A missing setting, or a hand-edited invalid one, must neither disable the guard nor wedge every channel.
- It never touches hopCounts or pausedChannels.
- Give it a short doc comment saying why: StateManager.load() re-applies chatMaxAgentHops on every FileWatcher reload, and building a new router there cleared every pause and hop count.
- Error handling: setMaxHops never throws.
- Leave the constructor signature and route() unchanged.

2) packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts, load(), about lines 1132-1133: replace the comment 'Re-initialize MentionRouter with project-configured maxHops' and the line that assigns a new MentionRouter with a one-line comment plus this.mentionRouter.setMaxHops(this.project?.settings?.chatMaxAgentHops);
- The constructor (about line 490) keeps new MentionRouter(4), so the router exists before the first load.
- The change is net zero lines. StateManager.ts must stay at split('\n').length 1483, under the 1500 budget that state/stateModules.test.ts enforces (mem:gotcha-statemanager-line-budget). Check with node -e before moving on.
- Touch nothing else in load(); its existing error handling and timeout stay as they are.

Out of scope:
- update_settings (state/profileRollout.ts updateProjectSettings) still applies a changed chatMaxAgentHops only at the next load(), exactly as today.
- No doc change: docs/SCHEMA.md already describes the pause-until-human behaviour this restores.
implementationPlan.note: setMaxHops added; load() calls it. StateManager.ts split-line count is 1483.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The chat loop guard (per-channel hop counts and pauses in MentionRouter) survives every StateManager.load(), including FileWatcher reloads. load() only re-applies settings.chatMaxAgentHops to the existing router. A missing or invalid value (anything but an integer >= 1) means the default, 4. Only a human message or the continue token resets a channel, as docs/SCHEMA.md states.
invariants: StateManager.ts split('\n').length stays below 1500 (state/stateModules.test.ts); this change is net zero lines.
The MentionRouter constructor signature, route(), resetChannel() and getChannelState() keep their current behaviour; system messages stay loop-guard neutral.
No schema, .moe file or MCP tool contract changes.
sourceAssumptions: state/StateManager.ts constructor (~490) builds new MentionRouter(4); load() (~1132-1133) rebuilds it from settings.chatMaxAgentHops.
index.ts (~848-853): the FileWatcher onChange calls healMassDeletion and then state.load().
util/mentionRouter.ts: hopCounts and pausedChannels are private maps on the instance; maxHops is readonly and set only by the constructor.
state/validators.ts bounds chatMaxAgentHops to an integer 1-20 on update_settings, but load() reads project.json unvalidated.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A maxHops setter on the existing router, called from load(). Chosen: the smallest change and net zero lines in the line-budgeted StateManager.ts. (2) Copying hopCounts and pausedChannels into a freshly built router. Rejected: it reaches into private state for no gain. (3) Rebuilding the router only when maxHops changes. Rejected: a changed setting would still drop every pause.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Three facts frame the fix:
- The router is constructed once in the StateManager constructor and again on every load(). The FileWatcher reloads on external .moe writes; state/sweeps.ts ~172-182 records that a claim reliably triggers one on the live host, which is the same reset-on-reload class the sweeps fix handled for timers.
- System messages are deliberately loop-guard neutral (util/mentionRouterSystemHops.test.ts).
- The repro is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-8f18d6fa/zzHuntUtil1.test.ts, including a real-FileWatcher case. Optional to reuse; its timing makes it unsuitable as a gate test.
planningNotes.risks:

- Never write a literal at-token in step text or a comment echoed to chat. Build it at runtime in tests.
- A lowered limit must apply to hop counts already accumulated: the next hop past the new limit pauses.
- Do not validate through validators.ts: another row holds that file. The integer >= 1 guard lives in setMaxHops.
